_comment: Site-type axis for the web-launch-readiness skill (road-to-web-launch-readiness 0.2). The design directive this file exists to enforce is CONDITIONAL, NOT FLAT: a check that applies everywhere is a check that gets ignored somewhere. Every entry declares which site types it applies to, so a SaaS app is never asked for opening hours and a docs site is never asked for a cookie banner it does not set. REGISTERED BEFORE ANY SKILL CODE EXISTS, which is the point of Phase 0: the axis is a decision, and deciding it after writing the checks would let the checks pick their own scope. Read today by loadConfig() in src/scripts/check_web_launch_readiness.ts and, through that checker, by the production-validator subagent; the checker itself stays default-off behind web_launch_readiness.enabled.

site_types._comment: The closed enum. A check may not name a type outside it, and a type carries no checks until one lists it -- so adding a type is inert until a check opts in, and removing one is caught by the schema test rather than silently emptying a check's scope.

tiers._comment: Report order, and it is the output contract rather than a label: critical first, situational last. A finding's tier is a property of the FINDING, not of the reader's patience -- a staging noindex on a production marketing site is critical whether or not the reader has time for it.

checks.title: A staging `noindex` or `robots.txt` disallow survived into production
checks.why: The defect class with ZERO coverage in the estate (G0: `robots` 0 files, `noindex` 0 files) and the highest cost: the site ships, works, looks correct, and is invisible to search. Nothing in the tree looks for it today.
checks.remediation: Remove the `noindex` meta tag and the blanket `Disallow: /` from the production build; keep them behind the staging environment's own config rather than in shared source.
checks.verification: `curl -sI <prod-url> | grep -i x-robots-tag` returns nothing, `curl -s <prod-url>/robots.txt` carries no blanket disallow, and the rendered HTML has no `noindex` meta.

basis.ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag (noindex, none) and https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/google-common-crawlers (Googlebot and Google-Extended tokens); crawler purposes per src/config/crawler-register.json

checks.title: HTTP is redirected to HTTPS and no asset is loaded over plain HTTP
checks.why: A mixed-content asset silently breaks the padlock and, on a form page, ships a credential over plaintext. Browsers block some of it and load the rest, so the page LOOKS fine while the guarantee is gone -- which is why this is critical rather than high.
checks.remediation: Serve every asset over https:// or protocol-relative paths, and redirect http:// at the edge. Never hard-code an http:// origin you control.
checks.verification: `curl -sI http://<prod-host>/` returns a 301/308 to https, and the browser console shows no mixed-content warning on the heaviest page.

basis.ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/mixed-content/ — browsers upgrade insecure images, audio and video and block other insecure subresources (Candidate Recommendation Draft, 2023-02-23)

checks.title: A custom 404 route exists and is reachable
checks.why: A framework default error page leaks stack shape and loses the visitor. `404` matches 19 files in the estate, all HTTP-status tables -- none is a launch check.
checks.remediation: Add the framework's custom 404 route and give it a link back into the site.
checks.verification: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <prod-url>/<random-path>` returns 404 and the body is the custom page, not the framework default.

basis.ref: Practice judgement: a framework default error page shows stack shape and loses the visitor. Estate evidence in `why`: `404` matches 19 files, none a launch check.

checks.title: Every indexable route carries a title and a meta description
checks.why: `meta description` matches 0 files. Excluded for `saas-app` and `internal-tool` on purpose: an authenticated app's routes are not indexed, so per-route descriptions are work with no consumer.
checks.remediation: Add title and description to each route's metadata export; a shared default is a fallback, not a per-route value.
checks.verification: Fetch each route in the sitemap and assert a non-empty, non-duplicated title and description.

basis.ref: Practice judgement: a shared or missing title and description on public routes. Estate evidence in `why`: `meta description` matches 0 files.

checks.title: Content images carry alternative text
checks.why: The one check that applies to every type, including internal tools -- an internal user with a screen reader is still a user. `alt text` matches 7 files, all accessibility prose rather than a launch check.
checks.remediation: Add `alt` to content images; decorative images take `alt=""` explicitly rather than being left without the attribute.
checks.verification: Parse the rendered HTML and assert every `` has an `alt` attribute, empty or not.

basis.ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html — SC 1.1.1; null alt on decorative images is sufficient technique H67

checks.title: Every page declares lang, charset and viewport
checks.why: A missing `lang` makes a screen reader guess the pronunciation of the whole page; a missing viewport makes a phone render a desktop layout at 320px. Both are one line, both are invisible on the developer's machine, and both are the kind of default a framework template silently drops when a page is hand-written.
checks.remediation: `<html lang="..">`, `<meta charset="utf-8">` and `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` in the shared layout, not per page.
checks.verification: View source on two unrelated routes and confirm all three are present on both -- one route proves the layout, two prove it is the layout and not a copy.

basis.ref: Practice judgement: lang, charset and viewport are one line each and invisible on the developer machine; no standards page is cited for this row.

checks.title: Canonical URLs, sitemap and robots.txt agree with each other
checks.why: Three sources that can disagree silently: a sitemap listing a route whose canonical points elsewhere, or a robots disallow on a route the sitemap advertises. Note `canonical` matches 115 files in this estate in a completely different sense ("the canonical rule"), so its count is NOT coverage evidence.
checks.remediation: Make the canonical the same URL the sitemap lists; remove sitemap entries that robots.txt disallows.
checks.verification: For each sitemap URL, fetch it and assert the canonical equals the sitemap entry and robots.txt does not disallow it.

basis.ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls — use absolute canonical URLs, do not give one page different canonicals or a sitemap URL that disagrees

checks.title: The legal pages the jurisdiction requires exist and are linked
checks.why: SITUATIONAL because the requirement is jurisdictional, not universal: a German commercial site needs an Impressum, a US one does not. The skill reports what is missing for the declared region and does not assert a legal conclusion -- that is the domain-safety-disclaimer boundary, not this file's.
checks.remediation: Add the pages the declared region requires and link them from the footer of every page.
checks.verification: Assert each declared-required page returns 200 and is reachable from the home page in one click.

basis.ref: The DE escalation row's `authority` in this file: DDG § 5 (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg/) and DSGVO Art. 13 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj); provenance, never counsel

checks.title: Analytics fires only after consent, where consent is required
checks.why: Also jurisdictional, and the failure is asymmetric: analytics that never fires costs data, analytics that fires before consent costs a regulatory exposure.
checks.remediation: Gate the analytics snippet behind the consent state; do not load it on first paint.
checks.verification: Load the page with consent declined and assert no request to the analytics origin.

basis.ref: Practice judgement: a measurement tag ordered before its consent gate; jurisdictional, and this row cites no statute.

checks.title: No third-party resource loads on first paint without the visitor's interaction
checks.why: SITUATIONAL because whether a first-paint request to a font, map, video or analytics provider needs the visitor's consent first is jurisdictional. The row states the load as a fact -- which origin, from which line -- and resolves the provider through the dated register src/config/third-party-origins.json; an origin missing from the register is reported undecided, never green.
checks.remediation: Self-host fonts and scripts, or put the embed behind a click-to-load placeholder that requests the provider only after an interaction. A `preconnect` to the provider opens a connection on its own and goes too.
checks.verification: Rebuild and re-run this check: the line is gone, and `--render` records no request to the origin on first paint.

basis.ref: src/config/third-party-origins.json evidence rows and the frozen ground truth tests/fixtures/third-party-load/ground-truth.json

checks.title: The imprint cites no provision the supersession table marks replaced
checks.why: SITUATIONAL because an imprint is jurisdictional. A model writing legal-page boilerplate reproduces the provision it saw most, which for a German imprint is the one replaced in May 2024; the supersession rows in this file carry the replacement, its effective date and the date they must be re-read by.
checks.remediation: Replace the citation with the provision the finding names, after checking the current text at the finding's authority.
checks.verification: Re-run this check: the imprint line no longer matches any supersession row.

basis.ref: The `supersessions` rows of this file, each with its own `authority` (tmg-5-to-ddg-5: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg/)

checks.title: Legal pages carry no unfilled template token
checks.why: SITUATIONAL because the legal pages themselves are. A bracketed slot such as `[Firmenname]` is a value nobody supplied; a numeric bracket is a footnote and is left alone.
checks.remediation: Fill every bracketed slot with the owner's real value, or remove the line.
checks.verification: Re-run this check: no bracketed word token remains in a located legal page.

basis.ref: Practice judgement: a bracketed word slot is a value nobody supplied; numeric brackets are footnotes and left alone.

checks.title: The privacy page names every provider the build loads
checks.why: SITUATIONAL because the privacy page is jurisdictional. The checkable half of a privacy notice is that every provider the page actually loads is named; this row compares the providers `third-party-load-in-markup` found loading with the located privacy page's text, and says nothing about the rest of the notice.
checks.remediation: Name each listed provider in the privacy page, or stop loading it.
checks.verification: Re-run this check: every provider found loading appears by one of its register names on the privacy page.

basis.ref: src/config/third-party-origins.json privacy_tokens and the frozen ground truth tests/fixtures/third-party-load/ground-truth.json

checks.title: An indexable page forbids its own search snippet (`nosnippet` / `max-snippet:0`)
checks.why: A page that is indexed but carries `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` is shown without a text snippet, and Google's guidance for its generative search features requires a page to be indexed and snippet-eligible. A leftover snippet block costs the listing its description while every presence check stays green.
checks.remediation: Remove `nosnippet` and `max-snippet:0` from the robots meta (or the crawler-named meta) of pages meant to appear in search; keep them only on pages whose text must not be quoted, and say so in the source.
checks.verification: The rendered HTML of each public page carries no robots or googlebot meta with `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0`, and `curl -sI <url> | grep -i x-robots-tag` shows neither directive.

basis.ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag — nosnippet, and max-snippet:0 as its equivalent

checks.title: A JSON-LD block does not parse
checks.why: A `<script type="application/ld+json">` block that is not valid JSON is ignored whole by every consumer, so the structured data the page claims to carry is not there. Only parsing is checked; which types a page declares, and how many, is not scored.
checks.remediation: Fix the JSON in the block (a trailing comma, an unescaped quote or a template placeholder are the usual causes) or remove the block; validate it with `JSON.parse` in the build.
checks.verification: Every `application/ld+json` block on the built pages parses with `JSON.parse`, and Google's Rich Results Test reads the page without a parse error.

basis.ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data — JSON-LD in a script tag is the recommended format; a block that is not JSON is not JSON-LD

not_in_scope._comment: Named so a later contributor does not add them by analogy. Performance budgets and Lighthouse scoring are a different instrument with a different failure mode (a score is a gradient, these checks are binary), and `lighthouse` matching 0 files is NOT an argument for adding it here. Accessibility beyond alt text belongs to accessibility-auditor, which already exists and does it properly.

no_import_decision._comment: Step 0.3, recorded HERE rather than in the skill body, and the relocation is a correction the step needs rather than a liberty taken. 0.3 sits in Phase 0, whose Exit condition reads "zero skill code written" -- so its verify line ("the decision is written in the skill's own body") names an artefact its own phase forbids. The decision is what the step is about; it is recorded in the earliest durable place that exists, and the skill body restates it at 2.1 when there is a body.
no_import_decision.rule: The external corpus is a STUDY OBJECT and a per-defect harvest source. Its rule set is not imported. Rules enter ONE AT A TIME, each against a named defect, each carrying its own remediation and verification.
no_import_decision.why: An imported rule set arrives with its authors' assumptions about site type, jurisdiction and stack, and none of those is checked on arrival. The failure is silent: the skill grows to N checks, each individually plausible, and the conditional axis this file exists to enforce is the first thing a bulk import flattens. One-at-a-time keeps the axis honest because every entry has to answer `applies_to` before it lands.
no_import_decision.ceiling_enforced_by: tests/scripts/web_launch_readiness_config.test.ts asserts checks.length < 50. The live count is NOT retyped here: a number a human retypes on every ledger edit drifts, and this field had said 7 while `checks` held 9. Read `checks.length`; the ceiling is the only number this row owns.

regions._comment: Region axis (road-to-web-launch-readiness 2.3). LEGAL-ROW CONTRACT: any row here or in `checks` whose `why` names a statute MUST carry `authority` (the citation and where it can be read) and `review_by` (the ISO date it must be re-read by); `authority` and `review_by` travel together, so a citation moved out of prose into `authority` stays dated; and a lapsed `review_by` FAILS the loader rather than warning, because a date nothing reads is a comment. Enforced by legalRowViolations() in src/scripts/check_web_launch_readiness.ts, which loadConfig() calls before returning. Separate from site_types because it answers a different question: site_types decides WHETHER a check applies, regions decides HOW SEVERELY. A DE-targeted site owes an Impressum and a Datenschutzerklaerung by law -- the citations sit in the escalation's `authority` field, dated, rather than in prose, which is what the `ddg-citation-authority` decision of 2026-09-03 settled -- so `required-legal-pages` is critical there and situational elsewhere -- the same check, a different tier. Modelled as a tier ESCALATION rather than as a second applies_to list, because a legal page is not more or less applicable in Germany, it is more or less optional.

escalations.why: A DE-targeted commercial site owes a published imprint and a privacy notice by law; the two citations and the date they must be re-read by live in this row's `authority` field, not in this sentence. Abmahnung risk is real and immediate, which is what separates critical from situational here.
escalations.authority: Impressum: DDG § 5 (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz), gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg -- in force since 2024-05-14, superseding the identically-numbered provision of the TMG, which is why the pre-2026-09-03 form of this row cited dead law: it was written on 2026-08-25, twenty-seven months after that supersession. Datenschutzerklaerung: DSGVO Art. 13, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, consolidated text at eur-lex.europa.eu. Both are cited here as provenance a reader can re-check, never as counsel: src/rules/legal-safety-floor.md governs how this package may speak about law, and `review_by` below is the date these two must be read again.

escalations.why: A DE-targeted site loading a provider before any interaction is the shape German courts have treated as a request needing the visitor's consent; the citation and its re-read date live in `authority` and `review_by`, not in this sentence.
escalations.authority: Consent before storage of or access to information in the visitor's terminal equipment: TDDDG section 25, gesetze-im-internet.de/ttdsg -- cited as provenance a reader can re-check, never as counsel; src/rules/legal-safety-floor.md governs how this package may speak about law.

escalations.why: A DE-targeted site owes the visitor a notice naming the recipients of their data; the citation lives in `authority`.
escalations.authority: Information to be provided to the data subject: DSGVO Art. 13, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, eur-lex.europa.eu. Cited as provenance, never as counsel.

escalations.why: Mirrors `required-legal-pages@de`: the imprint is owed by name there, and one citing replaced law is the defect a reader sees first.
escalations.authority: Imprint content: DDG section 5 (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz), gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg -- in force since 2024-05-14. Cited as provenance, never as counsel.

escalations.why: Mirrors `required-legal-pages@de`: an imprint whose provider slot reads `[Firmenname]` names nobody.
escalations.authority: Imprint content: DDG section 5 (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz), gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg -- in force since 2024-05-14. Cited as provenance, never as counsel.

supersessions.why: Superseded provision a page cites; one row per named defect (inbox-2026-11-g S1@00:24, corpus row 6). Further rows enter only with their own named defect.
supersessions.authority: Imprint content: DDG section 5 (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz), gesetze-im-internet.de/ddg -- in force since 2024-05-14. Cited as provenance, never as counsel.
